title: Admin orchestration lattice with safety validators and task emission
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight orchestration lattice that converts curated runbooks into a guarded, graph-executable flow and emits discrete support tasks when branching conditions require human intervention. This ticket covers the runtime executor, a small approval/safety validator layer, and a shim that allows existing admin utilities (CLI/HTTP) to invoke lattice graphs. Goal: reduce mean time to remediate (MTTR) for common operational scenarios while keeping strong permission and audit coloring for all automated actions.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can author a runbook as a directed graph YAML in the repo and deploy it to the lattice service
The lattice executor can run graphs with conditional branching, parallel nodes, and idempotent retries
When a node requires human approval, the system emits a Linear ticket with contextual metadata and a link back to the graph state
Safety validators (RBAC checks, secret usage audit, rate-limits) must run pre-execution and prevent execution if any validator fails
All actions and decision points are recorded in telemetry (trace id + token cost where applicable) and visible in Console traces
Automated regressions are prevented by a canary rollout (10% of internal incidents for two weeks) and a rollback hook on any post-deploy failure
technical_approach: Design a compact graph schema (YAML) with nodes typed as: builtin-utility, shell-wrapper, api-call, approval-gate, checkpoint
Implement Lattice executor as a stateless service that stores ephemeral execution state in Redis; final provenance is flushed to Postgres for audit
Safety validators run as a synchronous pre-flight stage; validators are pluggable (RBAC, KMS-usage, allowlist, rate-limit)
Task emission integrated with Linear API: emitted tasks include graph_id, node_id, snapshot of inputs, link to live trace, suggested assignees based on oncall rules
Provide a minimal CLI plugin (opsctl lattice run <graph>) and HTTP webhook endpoint for Console to trigger graphs with route-level permissions
Integrate with existing admin utilities by providing a stable gRPC mTLS shim to call executor internal APIs from on-prem operator agents
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal feature flag disabled; run playground graphs in dev; smoke tests against a staging Redis/Postgres
Phase 1: enable for SRE and Support teams behind feature flag; collect telemetry and feedback for 2 weeks
Phase 2: open to Infrastructure and selected internal customers; enable Linear task emission; cadence 10% Canary on real incidents
Phase 3: full rollout after 4 weeks of stable canary or after fixes; flip default safety validators to required
Rollback: immediate disable flag which drains new executions and allows in-flight runs to finish (cancel safe nodes)
testing_plan: Unit tests for executor state machine and node typing coverage
Integration tests: full graph execution with mock utilities and approval flows in CI
Chaos test: simulate Redis latency and Postgres failover to verify idempotency and retry semantics
E2E test with Linear test org to validate ticket emission and webhook acknowledgement
Security test: ensure KMS access is audited and validators block when keys are missing or mis-scoped
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: automated flows could perform destructive actions if validators are bypassed. Mitigation: require two independent validators for destructive node types and an immutable audit trail.
Risk: task spam if branching logic emits many tickets. Mitigation: dedupe emission by hash of event + window and provide ticket aggregation rules.
Risk: dependency on redis could lead to lost ephemeral state. Mitigation: lease-based heartbeats and write-ahead snapshots to Postgres every 30s.
Risk: opsctl plugin proliferation across environments. Mitigation: single binary distribution with env-aware configs and compatibility tests in our release pipeline.
